items.title: Proxmox ships with settings that waste power and disk space, and one cleanup fixes both
items.summary: Proxmox is a hypervisor built for always-on servers that never get a break from duty, and because of that, the defaults set when you install it on your home lab aren't necessarily the most optimal. On a fresh install it can hold your CPU at higher clocks than necessary and waste disk space on the SSD you boot from. For a home server or lab that idles the vast majority of the time that it's on, these small defaults can add up, but thankfully, saner settings are relatively easy to configure.

items.title: I tried 3 NAS operating systems to see if I could find a TrueNAS alternative
items.summary: TrueNAS has become almost synonymous with building your own NAS, and for good reason. It brings together ZFS, snapshots, replication, and a comprehensive web interface that makes managing even fairly complicated storage setups much easier. I like TrueNAS, but I have always wondered whether it is a little excessive for an ordinary home server. If all you want is somewhere to store files, back up your computers, and perhaps stream a few movies, do you really need everything it offers?

items.title: QRdx is an Open-Source QR Code Generator You Can Self-Host
items.summary: QR codes are everywhere, but finding a generator that offers decent customization without watermarks, mandatory accounts, or subscriptions can be surprisingly frustrating. Most tools handle basic URLs just fine, but things get complicated when you want custom designs, editable destinations, or a little more control over how your codes are managed. QRdx is an open-source QR code platform that brings these capabilities together in a single application. It offers a browser-based editor for creating customized QR codes, along with dynamic links, scan analytics, hosted landing pages, and several developer tools.

items.title: Posteryard Brings Clean, Consistent Posters to Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby

Some have oversized titles, others are covered in promotional text, and occasionally the artwork looks completely out of place next to everything else. Posteryard is a self-hosted, open-source tool that tackles this problem by automatically generating consistent artwork across your media library. Instead of manually choosing posters for hundreds of titles, it finds suitable artwork, applies a uniform layout, and keeps everything updated as your collection grows.

items.title: Debian 13.8 Released with 150 Security Updates and 122 Bug Fixes
items.summary: The Debian Project has announced the release of Debian 13.8, the eighth maintenance update to its stable Debian 13 “Trixie” series. items.title: Q&A: Enabling more human-like interactions and understanding in multimodal foundation models

Multimodal foundation models of artificial intelligence are increasingly gaining capabilities that mimic this.

items.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
items.summary: Modeling of complex, chaotic processes such as weather and climate patterns and turbulent flows in aviation or in ocean currents has advanced enormously in recent years. However, such models are still prone to drift into physically impossible predictions over time. Now, researchers with MIT’s Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) have found a way to introduce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models that can ensure that such models never exceed realistic bounds, based on what is actually possible in the real world.

items.title: A game you cannot win unless you have a quantum computer
items.summary: On a superconducting processor, we turned one of quantum mechanics’ strangest features into something you can measure, benchmark, and put to work across systems as large as 105 qubits. Here is a Sunday paper-style puzzle you can try right now. Draw a 3×3 grid. Fill every cell with either +1 or −1, subject to two rules: each row must multiply to +1, and each column must multiply to −1. You didn’t manage it, right? There is an elegant reason for that. For a row to multiply to +1, it needs an even number of −1s.

items.title: AI helps researchers investigate how thousands of medical studies share code
items.summary: The data and code that underpin a research study can tell us what was actually done, and how. In a medical study, for example, how were patients selected for inclusion? items.title: Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
items.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Vladimir Putin is a "killer" in response to Donald Trump referring to the Russian leader as his "friend" in China this week. items.title: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
items.summary: Efforts to set firm rules on AI-powered killer robots and drones ran aground Saturday as U.N.-backed talks in Geneva produced a softened agreement to extend discussions for two more years. Scores of countries ended the week-long U.N. conference on weapons by agreeing to "elaborate" a possible accord on such lethal autonomous weapons systems by 2028. But they didn't commit to binding rules sought by U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres, many countries, and activists. The outcome underscored the difficulty of achieving concrete results in diplomacy amid global conflicts and major military powers jockeying for dominance.

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine. In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate". He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsular it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use.

items.summary: TUCSON, AZ (AZFamily) — Volunteers with Humane Borders discovered one of the organization’s water stations had been destroyed near Arivaca, south of Tucson, leaving it unusable for people in need of water. items.title: The Brutal Ways Emperor Valerian Executed Early Roman Popes
items.summary: For much of the Christian Church’s history, the Papacy has been an office sought by many members of the clergy. But in the 3rd century, accepting the “keys to the kingdom” meant almost certain death, with up to three-fourths of those who ascended to the papal throne dying in all sorts of horrendous ways at the hands of Roman authorities. While many emperors are responsible for ordering the deaths of popes, Emperor Valerian has the distinction of murdering more popes than any other. The Rising Prestige of the Christian Church From the time of its inception, the early Christian Church operated underground, hoping to escape the attention of the Roman authorities.

items.title: Archaeologists Uncover Medieval Nubia’s Largest Cathedral
items.summary: Archaeologists working in Sudan have uncovered new sections of the largest cathedral in medieval Nubia, revealing a monumental staircase, walls still standing 11 metres high and the remains of a previously unknown church. The discoveries shed new light on the architectural achievements of the Christian Kingdom of Makuria. A Sudanese-Polish archaeological expedition working at Old Dongola has revealed further sections of the Great Church of Jesus, described in medieval Arabic sources as the largest and wealthiest church in Nubia.

items.summary: ADELAIDE – Two Virgin Australia (VA) pilots were removed from flying duties after reporting fatigue during a domestic flight from Melbourne (MEL) to Adelaide Airport (ADL) on November 18, 2026. items.summary: Gaining a pilot's license can be costly and prohibitive for many, including for those who just want to fly in a hang glider or ultralight aircraft. items.title: A New Jean-Michel Basquiat Documentary Considers the Artist Behind the Work
items.summary: A forthcoming documentary spotlights the life and work of luminary artist Jean-Michel Basquiat (1960-1988). Directed by Quinn Whitney Wilson and Viridiana Lieberman for Netflix, the feature film is the first project authorized by the artist’s two younger sisters, Lisane Basquiat and Jeanine Heriveaux, who helm his estate. In a trailer, the siblings describe their brother’s energetic approach to life and how the story typically told about his meteoric rise omits so much of who he really was. Simply titled Jean-Michel Basquiat, the film features archival footage and audio, along with never-before-seen works and commentary from his family.

items.title: Vatican Christmas Celebrations to Honour St. Francis of Assisi 800 Years After His Death
items.summary: The Vatican’s Christmas celebrations this year will commemorate the 800th anniversary of the death of St. Francis of Assisi, with a special ceremony linking St. Peter’s Square to the Italian town of Gubbio, famous for its medieval legend of the saint and a fearsome wolf. On 7 December, the Christmas tree in St. Peter’s Square will be illuminated simultaneously with the enormous Christmas tree display on Mount Ingino overlooking Gubbio. The ceremony will begin at 5:30 p.m., with children undergoing cancer treatment in Italian hospitals pressing the button to illuminate the Vatican tree.

items.title: How Magic Lantern Ghosts Helped Measure the Stars
items.summary: In the nineteenth century, entertainers began dazzling audiences with the “magic lantern.” Operators used these projection systems to bring marvelous images to large crowds. They even performed tricks on the eye, conjuring “ghosts” onto the stage using reflections or transparent screens. But some at the time saw scientific possibilities in those ghostly images. The rise of projection culture coincided with an increasing effort to mechanize astronomy. Astronomers had been precisely charting the positions of stars and other objects, and the next step was to study their color and brightness.

items.title: ‘We’re Still Here’ Celebrates Remarkable Quilts by 15 Contemporary Black Artists
items.summary: In the wee hours of a busy Saturday morning, on June 28, 1969, police raided The Stonewall Inn in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village, a renowned hangout for the LGBTQ+ community. During the 1950s and 1960s, few businesses openly welcomed gay people, and the legal system was against them—even two consenting adults in the privacy of their own home could face years in prison or a psychiatric institution if convicted of the crime of sodomy. Bar raids were common, but this one was particularly fraught due to the volume of people, and police quickly lost control.

items.title: Democrats Demand Answers From Oz After Delay in $50B Rural Health Awards
items.summary: Congressional Democrats are demanding answers and more transparency from the Trump administration after a nine-day delay of annual awards from a $50 billion fund meant to improve healthcare for rural Americans. The letter pointed to what it called “an alarming lack of public transparency” and said the fund “lacks sufficient guardrails to protect rural hospitals at greatest risk of closure.”

items.title: Elegance Flows Through Sheena Liam’s Embroideries in Green
items.summary: Model and ballet dancer Sheena Liam brings her understanding of poise, elegance, and graceful bodily movements to a more fixed medium. For the past several years, the artist has been stitching tender portraits of women with long, three-dimensional braids that cascade off the fabric. Occasionally, a single loose thread appears to have slipped out of its plait as it drifts across a protagonist’s cheek. Liam’s latest works are on view this month in her solo exhibition, The Unbearable Lightness. Several pieces feature figures sporting the same striped bodysuit with an open back, and the methodical pattern on the garment evokes both a sense of precision and rhythm depicted in the scenes.

items.title: Trafalgar Square Christmas tree felled in Norway
items.summary: This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London. The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old. It was felled on Friday by the Lord Mayor of Westminster, Karen Scarborough, and the Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe. Norway has sent a tree to the capital every year since 1947 as a thank you for Britain's support during World War Two, when King Haakon VII and the Norwegian government lived in exile in London.

items.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
items.summary: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025.

items.title: “Race realism” isn’t realistic—and it isn’t good science
items.summary: At this year’s World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, US President Donald Trump stated that people from Somalia have low IQs. “I always say these are low-IQ people,” he said in his speech. items.title: The libido drug women want is testosterone
items.summary: These days, Jessica Yih spends a lot of time talking to women about testosterone. Interest is “coming from all directions,” says the University of California, Irvine Health urologist. A major source: women who hope testosterone can boost the female libido. Only about a decade ago, women looking for libido treatments had few medical options — even though women of all ages struggle with low sexual desire. Some non-hormonal treatments are now available, but the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has yet to approve a female testosterone product, despite years of research suggesting it can boost sexual function and desire among postmenopausal women.

items.title: Preventable vision loss affects more than a billion people globally - and uneven access to care is the major culprit
items.summary: Around the world, more than 1 billion people are living with vision loss in their daily lives. For many, this means they don’t have the glasses they need to see clearly. For others, conditions such as cataracts, glaucoma, macular degeneration or diabetic eye disease have caused vision loss. The burden of this problem is not shared equally – 55% of those experiencing vision loss are women and girls, 73% are ages 50 and older, and 90% live in low- and middle-income countries. Age is the most important risk factor for vision loss.

items.title: HIDIVE Locks Down Release for 2027’s Biggest New Anime – Watch Trailer
items.summary: The Winter 2027 Anime season is right around the corner, and with it comes a massive slate of brand-new and returning series coming to global streaming giants. HIDIVE, one of the most popular anime streaming destinations in the world is premiering 2027’s biggest new comedy series, Giant Ojosama — also known as Giant Young Lady in English which will officially begin streaming during the Winter 2027 Anime season.

items.title: South Rim hotels reopen almost 3 months after flooding damaged Trans-Canyon Waterline
items.summary: GRAND CANYON (AZFamily) — Hotels at the Grand Canyon’s South Rim reopened Friday after being closed for nearly three months following deadly flash flooding that damaged the park’s main water pipeline. The hotels had been closed since the late August flooding, which forced dozens of people to evacuate the inner canyon and killed three men who were swept away by floodwaters. The flooding also caused extensive damage to the Trans Canyon Waterline, prompting Stage 4 water restrictions and the closure of overnight accommodations inside the park.

items.title: JetBrains Air in GoLand: Build, Review, and Profile Go Code With Agents
items.summary: If you’ve ever built backend services in Go, chances are you’ve also written a webhook handler or two. They’re small and rarely get much attention – that is, until something breaks. A third-party provider sends a signed request, and then you check the signature, store the event, and reply. Sounds like three easy steps, but a lot can go wrong. A captured request could get replayed, a duplicate could get saved twice, or a forged signature could slip through. Coding agents are not likely to make these types of mistakes, so with code becoming cheaper to generate, handlers are a good task to give them.

items.title: Tiny egg-eating snake discovered in Ethiopia
items.summary: Biologists have discovered multiple new species of egg-eating snakes slithering through the forests near southeastern Ethiopia’s Bale Mountains. Although researchers only described the white-throated egg-eater ( Dasypeltis albigularis ) in their study recently published in the journal Herpetozoa, they promised that information on additional finds is on the way. “Three other species in this genus are still waiting in line,” Arthur Tiutenko, a study co-author and herpetologist at Germany’s Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg (FAU), said in a statement.

items.title: Aspen Approves 60% Increase in GA Landing Fees
items.summary: Pitkin County commissioners have approved a 60% increase in general aviation landing fees at Aspen/Pitkin County Airport (ASE) for 2027. According to a county announcement Thursday, the new rates will rise from $13.76 to $22.04 per 1,000 pounds of aircraft weight as the airport prepares for a seven-month closure for runway reconstruction. Commissioners Reduce Proposed Increase The approved rates are lower than earlier proposals that would have raised GA landing fees by approximately 140%. County officials said airlines and general aviation operators had raised concerns about the proposed increases, prompting airport staff to develop a revised funding plan.

items.summary: Since the end of his HBO show Barry, some fans may have wondered, “ What’s Bill Hader been up to?” Yes, he voiced The Cat in the Hat, but he also wrote, directed, and is starring in a brand-new original horror movie, and soon we’ll get to see it. items.title: Fragmented Landscapes
items.summary: I don’t think it’s a surprise at this point when I tell you that I love these artworks by Antwerp-based artist Joost Vandebrug. (I mean, tell me they don’t aesthetically rhyme with the KDO logo circles/moons…) Joost Vandebrug explores how separate views and moments come to be seen as a whole. His landscapes gather fragments into places that feel familiar, even when no single place could contain them. The image takes shape through remembering and looking, while the joins keep its construction visible.

items.title: Lufthansa Ordered The Airbus A350-1000 In 2023 & Got It Before The Boeing 777-9 It Ordered In 2013
items.summary: Lufthansa is set to be the launch customer for the upcoming Boeing 777-9. The problem, however, is that it was scheduled to enter service in 2020. The entry-into-service date for the 777-9 has been pushed back several times, and the aircraft has become one of the most delayed projects in commercial aviation history. What's more, the 777-9 is not a new aircraft; rather, it's an overhaul of an existing aircraft type (albeit an extremely thorough one). The 777-9's EIS is now set for 2027.

items.title: F-35A Demo Team Moves Back To Luke AFB
items.summary: After moving to Hill AFB in 2019, the U.S. Air Force’s F-35A Lightning II Demo Team is now returning to Luke AFB, where it was originally created in 2016. The U.S. Air Force’s F-35A Lightning II Demonstration Team announced on Nov. 20, 2026, that it is preparing to return to Luke Air Force Base, Arizona. The team was initially created at Luke AFB in 2016 as F-35 Heritage Flight Team, before it was moved to Hill AFB, Utah, in 2019. The move to Hill AFB coincided with the transition of the team under Air Combat Command with the 388th Fighter Wing.

items.title: Army’s plan to blow up aging explosives will spread lead over part of Iowa – what you need to know about the risks
items.summary: The U.S. Army set off waves of anxiety in Iowa when it confirmed plans to carry out two controlled explosions at an ammunition facility there with just a few days’ notice. According to the Army, dozens of old barrels containing lead azide, an explosive used as a detonator, have become unstable and pose an “ unacceptable risk of accidental detonation.” Intentionally detonating the barrels is considered the best option for controlling the risk, the Army determined. However, the explosions are expected to release a large plume of lead particles, and lead is a neurotoxin.

items.title: When Your Winter Trip Has No Snow, Find Your Inner Daredevil Instead.
items.summary: I’ve never understood the appeal of roller coasters or similar thrill rides. The stomach-dropping plunges and screaming passengers who stumble off, then immediately get back in the perpetually long line? No, thank you. I’ve tried enough of them throughout my life to know they’re just not my thing. So imagine my surprise — or horror, or maybe a bit of both — when I found myself willingly, eagerly even, climbing into an Olympic bobsled, knowing I’d soon be barreling down an icy track at nearly 80 miles per hour, experiencing up to five times the force of gravity.

items.title: Two Boeing 747s Have Sat in Tunisia Since the Gulf War, Now Iraq Wants $1.8 Million
items.summary: TOZEUR – Iraq has reopened efforts to sell two Boeing 747 aircraft that have remained grounded in Tunisia for nearly 36 years, with Iraqi Airways (IA) setting a combined estimated value of $1.8 million. The aircraft, which were moved out of Iraq ahead of the 1991 Gulf War, have remained at Tozeur-Nefta International Airport (TOE) despite several attempts to resolve their ownership and financial complications. The Iraqi flag carrier published a new sale notice on November 18, 2026, offering both aircraft for $900,000 each.

items.title: Tecnam Flies Four People Into North America’s Highest Airport
items.summary: Tecnam recently completed a demonstration flight of its diesel-powered P2010 TDI to Lake County Airport in Leadville, Colorado, carrying four people to an airport nearly 10,000 feet above sea level. According to a company announcement Thursday, the aircraft departed Leadville after refueling and used less than half of the airport’s 6,400-foot runway during takeoff. Lake County Airport sits at an elevation of 9,934 feet, making it the highest public-use airport in North America. High-elevation airports present particular challenges for piston aircraft, especially when temperatures increase density altitude.

items.title: Texas, New Mexico Spaceports Propose 250-Mile Supersonic Flight Corridor
items.summary: Four organizations have signed a letter of intent to develop a dedicated supersonic flight testing corridor between Texas and New Mexico. The agreement, announced Wednesday, involves Midland Development Corporation, Midland International Air & Space Port, the New Mexico Spaceport Authority and Starfighters Space. The proposed corridor would extend approximately 250 nautical miles between Midland International Air & Space Port and Spaceport America, crossing sparsely populated areas of West Texas and southern New Mexico.

items.title: The Manufacturing Decision Boeing Was Forced To Make When It Developed The 737 MAX
items.summary: In August 2011, Boeing officially launched its 737 MAX program after American Airlines made the historic decision to split its once all-Boeing fleet and buy 50% of its next-generation narrowbodies from Airbus. AA was facing rising fuel expenses and operating an aging fleet of roughly 300 McDonnell Douglas MD-80 jets. Thus, in July of that same year, AA revealed that of the 460 jets it planned to procure to modernize its fleet, 260 would be from the A320 family.

items.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.summary: How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry. As frontier AI models become more capable, safeguards play an increasingly important role in how they can be used responsibly. Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards. An actor may use a frontier model’s outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities, then deploy it without comparable protections.

items.title: Iraq selling two Boeing 747s stranded in Africa for 35 years for $1.8 million
items.summary: Iraq is offering two Boeing 747s for sale for a combined $1.8 million after the aircraft spent 35 years parked at an airport in Tunisia, where they were flown for safekeeping ahead of the 1991 Gulf War. Iraqi Airways published a sale notice on November 18, 2026, valuing each aircraft at $900,000. Companies and individuals can submit offers for either airplane or both. The aircraft remain at Tozeur-Nefta International Airport in southwestern Tunisia. The pair comprises a Boeing 747-200 registered YI-AGP and a shorter-fuselage 747SP registered YI-ALM.

items.title: 4 Chain Restaurant Menu Items With Price Cuts In November 2026
items.summary: You know what's expensive these days? Everything, honestly, but food in particular. It's hard enough to go grocery shopping without running up an eye-watering tab, and fast food (which was previously cheap and tasty, if not necessarily healthy) is now considered a luxury. If you want to treat yourself to a sit-down meal, even at a chain restaurant? Well, just be careful out there. items.summary: Global Airlines has been forced into compulsory liquidation through something called a winding-up order. This order was given on November 4 and was confirmed in official public record about one week later.

items.title: What Makes Notre-Dame Cathedral a Masterpiece of Gothic Architecture
items.summary: Most of us remember where we were when we heard that Notre-Dame had burned down. And even upon learning that the most famous of all French cathedrals had been badly damaged rather than completely destroyed, it still felt as if something irreplaceable had been lost. It made no difference whether we’d actually been to the place, as I hadn’t at the time. When I did finally make it to Paris four years later, Notre-Dame’s restoration was still underway, and construction walls prevented anyone from seeing much of anything at ground level, let alone entering.

items.title: Salt Lake City Backs Down on Hangar Rent Hikes
items.summary: Salt Lake City International Airport has revised its planned hangar rent increases following objections from general aviation tenants and AOPA. Under the revised schedule, tenants will see their first increases in July 2027, followed by additional annual increases through 2030. The airport’s original plan called for monthly single-hangar rents to increase from $341 to $628 in January 2027 and then to $914 in July, representing a 168% increase over current rates. Under the revised schedule announced by AOPA on Thursday, rents will remain unchanged until July 1, 2027, when the monthly rate will increase to $487.63.

items.title: Veliki Kalnik Castle in Koprivnica, Croatia
items.summary: Above the village of Kalnik in northern Croatia, the walls of Veliki Kalnik Castle rise from a jagged rocky ridge. Built across several levels, the medieval stronghold follows the natural contours of the rock, making its surviving towers and walls appear to grow out of the mountain. First documented in 1243, the castle is best known for a story involving King Béla IV of Hungary and Croatia. According to local legend, the king took refuge here during the Mongol invasion of the 13th century. As the siege dragged on and supplies dwindled, villagers kept the defenders fed with plums.

items.title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
items.summary: The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards. While a typical PC board has about 12 layers of tracks, AI server boards can have 40 to 60 layers or more, and each additional layer requires more resin, copper foil, and laminate.

items.title: The Crucified Tongkonan of Tolu Deri in North Toraja Regency, Indonesia
items.summary: In the highland villages of North Toraja, the skyline is dominated by tongkonan —traditional ancestral houses with sweeping, boat-shaped saddle roofs that loom dramatically over the landscape. For centuries, these wooden structures have served as the spiritual and social anchor for Torajan clans, decorated strictly according to Aluk Todolo ("the way of the ancestors"), the indigenous animist belief system. Their facades are traditionally adorned with carved geometric patterns ( pa'ssura' ), water buffalo horns ( kabongo' ), and sculpted wooden heads ( katik ) symbolizing wealth, status, and protection.

items.title: Signal now blocks screenshots by default to stymie AI agents
items.summary: The company is calling for a simple way for developers to opt out of AI snooping. Signal views AI agents built into phones as an "existential threat," and it's acting accordingly. The encrypted messaging app said Friday that it will block screenshots by default on iOS 27, and on Android when AI assistants try to capture the screen. The measures keep Apple's Siri AI and Google's Gemini Intelligence from snooping on your chats, at least to a degree. The assistants are designed to help users by reading what's on the screen and pulling in information to better answer their questions.

items.summary: TikTok addicts can now doomscroll videos about LibreOffice, which now has an official account on the platform. items.title: Archer teams with Disney on aviation research, unveils Avengers-themed air taxi
items.summary: Archer Aviation has teamed with Walt Disney Imagineering’s research and development arm to explore future transportation concepts, marking the announcement with an Avengers-themed electric aircraft at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. The companies announced the collaboration on November 19, 2026. Archer’s Midnight electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft appeared at the event wearing Disney branding and a custom livery promoting Marvel Studios’ upcoming film Avengers: Doomsday. Archer described the work with Disney Imagineering as “early, exploratory research,” with the teams planning to examine technical concepts and potential passenger experiences.

items.title: I Walked Solo Along England’s Rugged South West Coast Path for Three Days
items.summary: I’m standing atop a spit of land jutting out into the English Channel, peering down at a beach accessible only by boat, where a small group of sunbathers lounge on the rocky sand. The view is a welcome excuse to catch my breath before continuing along five more rolling cliffs—400 steep feet up, 400 steep feet down, and repeat. And so, despite my exhausted legs and the blister that’s forming over my right big toe, I decide to imprint this impossibly peaceful scene into my brain to remind myself why I’m doing this trip.

items.title: Our Editors Test Tons of Gear. We’re Still Using These 22 Items Years Later.
items.summary: Our Writers Test Tons of Gear. These Are the 22 Items We’re Still Using. g a snapshot in time — an editor tested a new piece of luggage on a flight or wore a waterproof jacket on a few rainy camping trips. So when you’re someone who writes gear reviews, you have a lot of gear. Some is randomly mailed to you in the hopes you’ll like it and write about it, and there’s plenty we buy, because different types of travel call for different types of gear (and we travel whenever we can). Some gear stays in our closets, some gets donated, and some doesn’t quite live up to the hype, so we don’t write about it at all.

items.title: Incoming Democratic leader promises a more respectful Arizona Legislature
items.summary: It will be a whole new world in the coming year with Democrats at the helm of the Arizona Legislature, and one of the favorite punching bags for Republicans at Capitol is hopeful that will mean a shift toward collegiality. “By God, I hope it changes the tone,” Jen Marson, executive director of the Arizona Association of Counties, said during a Wednesday Zoom discussion hosted by Arizona State University’s Mechanics of Democracy Lab. Marson has spent the last 20 years advocating for Arizona’s 15 counties at the state legislature.

items.title: Google Donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to Secure AI Agents at Scale
items.summary: Google has announced it is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), placing two important components of its AI agent infrastructure under vendor-neutral open-source governance. The move is intended to address two emerging challenges in running autonomous agents at scale: securely executing untrusted, AI-generated code and managing the substantial compute overhead created by agents that frequently pause and resume. The announcement also includes OpenRL, Google's open-source reinforcement learning orchestration project.

items.title: GTA 6 sales hit $3.8bn in a single day - the biggest entertainment launch in history
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to be the biggest entertainment launch in history after the blockbuster video game debuted on Thursday, following a 13-year wait. Internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare said PS5 downloads in the UK peaked at 8.6 times normal levels around its launch. New Zealand, where GTA 6 was first available, saw a 14.8-fold spike four hours before, suggesting some players switched regions for early access. Pre-orders and first-day sales totalled more than 24.5 million units, making about $2.36bn (Â£1.8bn), according to analytics site Sensor Tower.

items.summary: You know your way around a classic holiday turkey. You know how to thaw turkey in advance and then cook it to golden perfection. items.title: The Best Places to Go in Central and South America 2027
items.summary: This is my fourth year leading our guide to the Best Places to Go in Central and South America, and each time I’m in awe of the final result—our list for 2027 is no exception. We’re talking about a region where the Pacific, the Atlantic, and the Caribbean converge; where the Andes reach for the Amazon; and where strings of puffy volcanoes and postcard-worthy islands stud the map like jewels. Within it all there are thriving cities where cultures ancient and modern collide head-on, and small towns that are timeless in a way that feels increasingly rare.

items.summary: Despite the president’s attacks, Sea Services is training New England fishers in offshore wind construction and providing them with a second income stream On a rainy September morning, the Pamela Ann, a rusty, 86ft (26-metre) scallop boat, docked in New Bedford, Massachusetts. The two-way main zipper, helmet-compatible hood, and large internal mesh pockets are useful climbing-oriented details, though our assessment centered on the features and fit rather than a documented high-altitude trip.

items.summary: Agentic AI can speed up velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows. Healthy code makes AI perform better and costs fewer tokens. Safeguarding means keeping code health high through agentic refactoring, with an MCP supplying code health data, so AI can maintain the code it generates. By Ben Linders…

items.title: OpenAI brings its collaborative Space hubs to Plus users
items.summary: You can upload documents, files and more to the hubs for easy sharing. Back at its Dev Day event in September, OpenAI debuted ChatGPT Space. It's a hub that allows you, your coworkers or friends and any Dot agents you've set up to share information and collaborate on documents and other files. On release, ChatGPT Space was available to users on the company's Pro, Business and Enterprise plans. Now, OpenAI is expanding availability to those paying for its $20 per month Plus subscription. If you're one those people, you can create your own Spaces starting today.

items.title: Katabatic Gear Tarn Down Jacket Review
items.summary: Bottom Line The Katabatic Gear Tarn ( men’s / women’s ) is a useful ultralight insulating layer for backpackers who want warmth at a manageable price. At 10.6 ounces in a men’s medium, it weighs almost exactly as much as the UL Mountain Hardwear Ghost Whisperer, but costs substantially less. We found the athletic shoulder cut comfortable for overhead movement and liked the adjustable hood, hem, and two internal drop pockets. The Tarn isn’t trying to be a heavy-duty winter parka. Its 3.6 ounces of down provide respectable warmth for the weight, but we rely on it for three-season backpacking, summer thru-hikes, and as an insulating layer under a shell.

items.title: Welcome Inkling 2 Mini, Cutting-edge Performance for your Local Setup
items.summary: TLDR; Inkling 2 Mini is a new looped transformer model. It’s a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts with ~26B physical total and 3B active parameters per token. It uses a neat trick to increase capacity: some layers are visited in a loop that repeats three times, which makes it work like it had more parameters. It supports a 1M-token context size, accepts images and text inputs. Thinking Machines Lab ships the model in a mixed-precision format, with NVFP4 and MXFP8 expert weights. A DSpark drafter is also included for additional speed-up at a small memory cost.

items.title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost
items.summary: Combining RL on a custom task distribution with your favorite agent harness yields more accurate and efficient models for that target harness and task distribution. Models are not fully optimized for all harnesses and the tasks you’re doing. Instead, they target general performance. So when you combine a model and harness, you’re leaving performance and efficiency on the table for the stuff you’re actually doing. With RL, you can train a custom harness adapter that squeezes everything out of your model for your harness and task combination.
